body:
## Summary

`resolveExitReason()` and `resolveMemoryExhaustion()` in `js/src/lib/exit-reason.js` (start-command 0.35.1, still on `main`) treat Docker's `State.OOMKilled` as proof that **the command** ran out of memory, whatever its exit code. Since moby/moby#43564, that flag is container-wide and sticky: it is set as soon as **any** process in the container cgroup is OOM-killed, and it is cleared only when the container starts again.

So when a child process (here a `rustc` inside `cargo test`) is OOM-killed, and the main command keeps running and later exits `1` for an unrelated reason, `$ --status` reports:

```
exitCode 1
oomKilled true
exitReason memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)
memoryExhausted true
memoryExhaustedReason Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true
```

Consumers then show "memory exhaustion" as the reason the command exited. In link-assistant/hive-mind#2498, the command actually stopped about 8 minutes after the OOM event because a Claude OAuth session expired. The pull request still got a notice saying `$ --status reports memory exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)`.

#178 fixed the same assumption in `isKilledExit()` / `--on-kill-resume`. These two functions were not changed.

## Reproduction

```js
// npm pack start-command@0.35.1 && tar xzf start-command-0.35.1.tgz
const { resolveExitReason, resolveMemoryExhaustion } = require('./package/src/lib/exit-reason.js');
for (const [exitCode, oomKilled] of [[0, true], [1, true], [1, false], [137, true], [137, false]]) {
  console.log(exitCode, oomKilled, resolveExitReason({ exitCode, oomKilled }), JSON.stringify(resolveMemoryExhaustion({ exitCode, oomKilled })));
}
```

Output:

```
exit=0 oomKilled=true -> exitReason="memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)" memory=null
exit=1 oomKilled=true -> exitReason="memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)" memory={"memoryExhausted":true,"memoryExhaustedReason":"Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true"}
exit=1 oomKilled=false -> exitReason=null memory=null
exit=137 oomKilled=true -> exitReason="memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)" memory={...}
exit=137 oomKilled=false -> exitReason="signal (SIGKILL)" memory=null
```

Real-world container footer (full log: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/e653eed6994482185e30cf4fc6803272/raw/a2e204b9e3ba9a58014f12872bc0e2015f6a8f22/tmp-start-command-logs-isolation-docker-d9c55596-ba34-4d9a-bd29-a3403c2c191f.log.txt):

```
Exit Code:  1
OOMKilled:  true
Reason: exitCode=1 oomKilled=true
```

The log shows `(signal: 9, SIGKILL: kill)` for a `rustc` child at 19:38, then `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed` at 19:40, then exit 1 at 19:41.

## Expected

The sticky flag alone should count as memory exhaustion of the command only when the command itself died by a signal: exit code 137 (`128 + SIGKILL`), or, more generally, `>= 128` / a signal exit. Same rule as `isKilledExit()` after #178. For an ordinary exit (`0`, `1`, `2`, …), `oomKilled` should stay a separate observation ("a process in the container was OOM-killed"), not the exit reason.

## Suggested fix

```js
// resolveExitReason
if (input.oomKilled === true && signalNameForExitCode(input.exitCode) === 'SIGKILL') {
  return 'memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)';
}

// resolveMemoryExhaustion
if (input.oomKilled === true && signalNameForExitCode(exitCode) === 'SIGKILL') {
  return { memoryExhausted: true, memoryExhaustedReason: 'Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true' };
}
```

Log-marker detection (`detectMemoryMarker` / `detectExitReason`) can stay as it is: those markers are evidence written by the command itself. Optionally, add a separate field such as `oomEventInContainer: true` (or keep relying on `oomKilled`) so consumers can still warn that a child process was OOM-killed.

## Workaround (consumer side)

hive-mind (link-assistant/hive-mind#2498) recognises `memoryExhaustedReason === 'Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true'`, and `exitReason === 'memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)'` without a reason, as a restatement of the sticky flag. It folds them into its own `oomKilled` handling and does not report them as independent evidence of memory exhaustion.

## References

- moby/moby#43564: "A container's `State.OOMKilled` flag is now set to true immediately upon any container process getting OOM-killed by the kernel, and cleared to false when the container is restarted"
- #178: same root cause in `--on-kill-resume`
- link-assistant/hive-mind#2498: the incident and case study
title: `$ --status` reports `memoryExhausted` / `exitReason: memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)` for an ordinary exit 0/1 when the sticky `OOMKilled` flag is set
